heard: a $125 million orbiter vanished because of a simple unit error. Launched in 1998, the probe spent nine months traveling to Mars. In September 1999, the probe reached its destination and prepared to enter orbit. But instead of sliding into a safe path, the spacecraft went silent and never called home. Investigators found a lethal software conflict between NASA and the builder, Lockheed Martin. One team used metric newtons, while the other used imperial pounds, a 4.45 times difference. This math error steered the probe into the Martian atmosphere at an altitude of just 57 kilometers. Dropping below 80 kilometers destroyed the orbiter. That was the survival limit. A simple unit error meant a $125 million orbiter vanished.
